comment: Plain-English headlines + summaries per motion, generated by `python -m ingest.summarize_motions` and merged into docs/data*.json by build_dataset. Keyed by a content hash of the motion (see summarize_motions.motion_key) — NOT by motion id, which renumbers. Safe to hand-edit: a corrected entry is never overwritten unless you pass --force.

0165ae9da625336a.headline: Chapel and recreation development agreement
0165ae9da625336a.summary: Ahead of the site plan, the commission recommended that the council approve the development agreement for the Eagle Mountain chapel and recreation building.
0165ae9da625336a.impact: Nothing is signed until the council votes. The site plan the commission recommended the same night depends on this agreement clearing the council first.

02e2b6772876c281.headline: Chapel and recreation building site plan
02e2b6772876c281.summary: The commission backed the site plan for the Eagle Mountain chapel and recreation building on two conditions: the development agreement passes first, and the lighting plan meets city standards.
02e2b6772876c281.impact: Neighbors of the site will see no construction on the strength of this vote. The council still has to sign off, and the applicant has to bring its lighting plan into compliance.

034d9672198c8045.headline: May 26 minutes approved
034d9672198c8045.summary: The commission approved its May 26 minutes after correcting the record to list Commissioner Jensen as the alternate commissioner.
034d9672198c8045.impact: A title fix in the meeting record, made by the commission itself. Nobody outside the room feels this one.

0af5ff7ee63ab740.headline: Change to the final plat rules
0af5ff7ee63ab740.summary: The commission asked the council to change the city's code section governing final plats for subdivisions.
0af5ff7ee63ab740.impact: Surveyors and developers filing subdivision paperwork are the ones who work in this section. For everyone else it is invisible, and the council has yet to vote on it.

104e1f51d74f36cf.headline: Annexation policy plan
104e1f51d74f36cf.summary: Commissioners took up the city's annexation policy plan, the document that sets which land Eagle Mountain may take in, and sent it toward the council.
104e1f51d74f36cf.impact: The minutes do not record how the vote came out. Annexation shapes the city's future boundaries, so this one is worth watching when the council picks it up.

1215b675e78a6a26.headline: Cost estimate rules for subdivision work
1215b675e78a6a26.summary: The commission asked the council to update the code sections covering cost estimates for subdivision and development work.
1215b675e78a6a26.impact: The council makes the call at a later meeting. Engineers and developers pricing out required improvements would feel this; a homeowner would not.

2c0fd66a7bc21a30.headline: Taller screening plants along parking lots
2c0fd66a7bc21a30.summary: The commission backed new landscape and buffering rules, rewriting one line to require a continuous 3.5-foot-tall wall of plants to block headlights.
2c0fd66a7bc21a30.impact: Developers planting new parking areas would have to put in trees, shrubs or grasses tall enough at planting to hide headlights from neighbors. The council decides whether it becomes law.

2d774f78f8f3bd6e.headline: Brandon Park zoning change moves to council
2d774f78f8f3bd6e.summary: The commission recommended the council approve a zoning change for Brandon Park.
2d774f78f8f3bd6e.impact: A zoning change decides what can be built on the land, so neighbors have reason to follow it. Acreage and the new zone are not in the record here, and the council still has to vote.

31df220494676928.headline: Retaining wall variance denied on Wright property
31df220494676928.summary: The commission turned down a request to bypass the city's retaining wall rules, finding the lot has room for a tiered wall meeting standards.
31df220494676928.impact: The owner must build to the city's tiered wall standard rather than the wall proposed. Sloped ground on its own will not win a variance, which matters to anyone with a hillside lot.

3a737e20aabcd93d.headline: Chapel and rec building site plan shelved
3a737e20aabcd93d.summary: The site plan for the Eagle Mountain Chapel and Recreation Building was set aside by the commission for a later meeting.
3a737e20aabcd93d.impact: The plan sits where it is until the commission picks it up again. Nobody's property or paperwork changes in the meantime.

41ca21da03d3e853.headline: Spring Run Plaza plat held to April 28
41ca21da03d3e853.summary: A decision on the preliminary plat for Spring Run Plaza was pushed to the commission's April 28, 2026 meeting.
41ca21da03d3e853.impact: Two more weeks before anything is decided about this project. If you want to weigh in, the item comes back at the end of the month.

481986547e66d9a3.headline: Change to the residential standards table
481986547e66d9a3.summary: The commission recommended that the council amend the residential standards table in the zoning code, without stating in the motion what the change alters.
481986547e66d9a3.impact: The motion does not say which standards move, so there is nothing yet to tell homeowners what they could build differently. The council decides whether it takes effect.

4ac9165d616ce233.headline: First-stage plat for Spring Run Plaza
4ac9165d616ce233.summary: Backing the site's lot layout, the commission sent the Spring Run Plaza preliminary plat to the council, conditioned on a signed agreement and the extended turn lane.
4ac9165d616ce233.impact: This is the lot layout step, and it holds until the council acts and the agreement is signed. Builders on that site are watching; nobody else needs to.

4b782929b3b334ac.headline: Stricter screening rules for HVAC equipment
4b782929b3b334ac.summary: The commission asked the council to change the city's HVAC screening rules: allow polyethylene, drop landscaping as an option, and require screens within 6 inches of the ground.
4b782929b3b334ac.impact: Nothing changes yet, the council votes on this later. If it passes, anyone installing air conditioning equipment would have to box it in rather than hide it behind plants, and paint the connecting lines to match the wall.

5ba14bd0fa5a3505.headline: June 23 minutes approved
5ba14bd0fa5a3505.summary: The commission signed off on the minutes of its June 23, 2026 meeting.
5ba14bd0fa5a3505.impact: This is the housekeeping that makes the written record of that meeting official. You will not feel it anywhere.

6196574fec3fbfb7.headline: March minutes fixed and approved
6196574fec3fbfb7.summary: The commission approved its March 24, 2026 minutes after correcting the record to show Commissioner Hess led the Pledge of Allegiance.
6196574fec3fbfb7.impact: Housekeeping that makes the last meeting's record official. Nobody outside the meeting room feels it.

6508d7f295d4ff28.headline: Angel's Landing lot split approved
6508d7f295d4ff28.summary: The commission approved the Angel's Landing lot split, dividing the property into separate lots; the motion records neither the acreage nor how many lots result.
6508d7f295d4ff28.impact: This one the commission settled itself, with no council vote to follow. It redraws lot lines at Angel's Landing and touches the owner and immediate neighbors, not the wider city.

675e0a11f004e415.headline: July 14 minutes fixed and approved
675e0a11f004e415.summary: The commission approved its July 14 minutes after correcting Commissioner Hess's recorded vote from yes to abstain.
675e0a11f004e415.impact: The official record now shows how Commissioner Hess voted that night. Beyond that file, nobody's day changes.

67cab1f229d9f8df.headline: Seasonal political sign rules
67cab1f229d9f8df.summary: Commissioners backed changes to the city's rules on seasonal political signs, with one clerical error corrected before it moves to the council.
67cab1f229d9f8df.impact: If the council agrees, the rules for putting campaign signs on your property around an election would change. Nothing is in force yet.

6a9e1cd424c21947.headline: July 28 minutes approved with a correction
6a9e1cd424c21947.summary: The commission approved its July 28, 2026 minutes after fixing the record to show Commissioner Hess made the motion on Item 7.A.
6a9e1cd424c21947.impact: A correction to the written record of a past meeting. It touches the file the city keeps and nothing you will encounter.

6b0263cd701a145d.headline: March 10 minutes approved
6b0263cd701a145d.summary: The commission signed off on the written record of its March 10, 2026 meeting.
6b0263cd701a145d.impact: Bookkeeping that makes the last meeting's record official. Nothing here reaches a resident.

7234a264346bab4e.headline: Variance denied for Pony Express Business Park
7234a264346bab4e.summary: The commission refused to waive the wash setback, retaining wall and drive-through circulation rules for the Pony Express Business Park site.
7234a264346bab4e.impact: Whoever builds there has to meet the standard setback, wall and drive-through rules or come back with a redesign. The commission found the lot still holds room for a workable commercial building. Nothing changes for anyone who does not build on that property.

738bb7b5e19d8365.headline: Flagship development agreement sent to council
738bb7b5e19d8365.summary: The commission asked the City Council to approve a development agreement for Flagship, the terms of which the motion does not spell out.
738bb7b5e19d8365.impact: Nothing is settled yet: the council takes the final vote. The record here gives no location, acreage or unit count, so what it would build is not something this motion tells you.

7442cacfb274e6af.headline: Fee schedule sent to council with two fixes
7442cacfb274e6af.summary: The commission backed the city's consolidated fee schedule, asking that a 180-day deposit-holding line be struck and an unfinished footnote be completed.
7442cacfb274e6af.impact: The fee schedule sets what you pay the city for permits and inspections. Nothing changes yet: the council takes the final vote, and these two edits are cleanup rather than new charges.

7b0e8d66b37f817f.headline: Senior housing overlay zone recommended
7b0e8d66b37f817f.summary: The commission backed a new senior housing overlay zone, with accessory dwelling units barred inside it and five rural zones cut off from density bonuses.
7b0e8d66b37f817f.impact: If the council agrees, builders could add senior housing at higher density in some areas, though not in the RA1, RA2, RD1, RD2 or FR zones. Renting out a basement apartment would be off limits in these developments.

807ed236563569d2.headline: Transportation plan and road impact fees
807ed236563569d2.summary: The commission recommended the council adopt the city's transportation master plan and the impact fee facilities plan that goes with it, with changes noted by David Salazar.
807ed236563569d2.impact: Impact fees are what builders pay toward new roads, so this plan sits behind those fee amounts. The council sets both, and until it votes, nothing changes for drivers or homebuyers.

8e1f5b66a037e1b3.headline: Scenic Mountain zoning change recommended
8e1f5b66a037e1b3.summary: The commission asked the City Council to approve the Scenic Mountain rezone; the motion names no acreage, location, or new zoning district.
8e1f5b66a037e1b3.impact: Land use does not change until the council votes. Residents who care what gets built there should follow the item to that meeting.

8f65c672f58b85b7.headline: Stadion development deal change sent to council
8f65c672f58b85b7.summary: The commission backed a first amendment to the Stadion development agreement and passed it to the City Council for the final vote.
8f65c672f58b85b7.impact: Nothing changes on the ground from this vote. The council takes it up later and can decide otherwise.

91b547edb2d8eb94.headline: June 9 minutes approved
91b547edb2d8eb94.summary: The commission approved the written record of its June 9, 2026 meeting.
91b547edb2d8eb94.impact: Housekeeping for the clerk's file, and nothing more.

9450bb25439878cb.headline: Pinnacles zoning change sent to the council
9450bb25439878cb.summary: The commission asked the City Council to approve the Pinnacles zoning change and an amendment to the master development plan agreement for the site.
9450bb25439878cb.impact: Nothing changes on the ground yet. The council holds the final vote and can decide otherwise, so if you live near the Pinnacles site, that is the meeting to watch.

a045dc56e11b8812.headline: Master site plan rules, result unrecorded
a045dc56e11b8812.summary: Commissioners took up a change to the city code section on master site plans and moved to recommend it to the council; the minutes do not record the result.
a045dc56e11b8812.impact: Master site plans are a developer's step, not yours. With no result written down, it is not clear this recommendation ever reached the council at all.

aa75b5bc3cb74488.headline: Drive-through and parking garage rules advance
aa75b5bc3cb74488.summary: City code covering drive-throughs and structured parking would be rewritten under an amendment the commission sent to the council unchanged.
aa75b5bc3cb74488.impact: Anyone designing a drive-through restaurant or a parking structure would build to the new standards. The council has not voted, and the motion does not describe what the standards say.

b34adc563576f11a.headline: Chapel development agreement put on hold
b34adc563576f11a.summary: The commission postponed the development agreement for the Eagle Mountain Chapel and Recreation Building without acting on it.
b34adc563576f11a.impact: No decision was reached about the chapel project. The motion sets no return date, so the record does not say when the item comes back.

c476a124bbe8455f.headline: April 14 minutes approved
c476a124bbe8455f.summary: The commission approved the minutes of its April 14 meeting.
c476a124bbe8455f.impact: Housekeeping for the record: it makes the account of that meeting official. Nothing here reaches your street.

d420a76af46588dc.headline: Brylee Townhomes agreement change backed
d420a76af46588dc.summary: A first amendment to the Brylee Townhomes development agreement won the commission's support, with the decision left to the City Council.
d420a76af46588dc.impact: The council has the last word here, so the amendment is not in force. Neighbors of the townhome site will see no change from this step.

d4a6cc9a24193ea3.headline: Pinnacles rezoning sent to the council
d4a6cc9a24193ea3.summary: The commission asked the City Council to approve a zoning change for the Pinnacles property, without recording the acreage or the new zone in the motion.
d4a6cc9a24193ea3.impact: Nothing about the site changes yet: the council votes later and can decide otherwise. If you live near Pinnacles, that council meeting is the one to watch.

d521ded6e0063127.headline: Triumph development agreement change
d521ded6e0063127.summary: The commission recommended a second amendment to the Triumph master development agreement, which sets the terms for that development.
d521ded6e0063127.impact: The record does not say what the amendment changes. Neighbors of the Triumph project are the ones with a reason to follow it to the council.

d52395b3fa9c3fe6.headline: Backyard recreation buildings
d52395b3fa9c3fe6.summary: Over one commissioner's objection, the commission recommended a new code section on accessory recreation buildings.
d52395b3fa9c3fe6.impact: This governs what you may build on your own lot alongside your house, such as a detached recreation structure. The council has the final say.

d909ead1ce6fee59.headline: May 12 minutes approved
d909ead1ce6fee59.summary: The commission signed off on the written record of its May 12, 2026 meeting.
d909ead1ce6fee59.impact: This one lives in the clerk's files. It makes the record of the last meeting official and asks nothing of you.

e0bf75b4109ae2da.headline: Change to the preliminary plat rules
e0bf75b4109ae2da.summary: Commissioners also sent up a change to the code section on preliminary plats, the earlier stage of the same subdivision review.
e0bf75b4109ae2da.impact: Another one aimed at the people who file subdivision plans. Nothing here reaches your street, and the council decides whether the wording changes at all.

e96bc40b9c7c5462.headline: Concept plan rules put off to May
e96bc40b9c7c5462.summary: The commission delayed a decision on the city's concept plan rules until its May 12 meeting.
e96bc40b9c7c5462.impact: The existing rules stay in place until then. Only people filing concept plans have a reason to follow this one.

f1f74eeb0b08c5b9.headline: Setback rules along the wildlife interface boundary
f1f74eeb0b08c5b9.summary: The commission backed a code change moving the setback from the rear lot line to the wildlife urban interface boundary, and applying it to homes and outbuildings.
f1f74eeb0b08c5b9.impact: Owners whose lots touch that boundary would measure the setback from the boundary, not the back property line, and outbuildings would count too. The council has the final say.

f40bdad2faef43bf.headline: Spring Run Plaza development deal sent to council
f40bdad2faef43bf.summary: The commission recommended the Spring Run Plaza master development agreement, asking that the right turn lane be extended to the service drive.
f40bdad2faef43bf.impact: Nothing is built on this yet: the council votes later. Neighbors of the site and drivers turning in are the ones who would notice, with a longer turn lane feeding the plaza's service drive.

f5cdc45b2d1565de.headline: Eagle Quest development agreement amendment
f5cdc45b2d1565de.summary: The commission asked the council to approve a second amendment to the Eagle Quest master development agreement.
f5cdc45b2d1565de.impact: Master development agreements set the terms a builder must follow on a large project. The record here gives no detail on what the amendment changes, and the council has not voted on it.

fe2baf437c027acc.headline: Barbed wire fence rules, numbering fixed
fe2baf437c027acc.summary: Commissioners sent the council a change to the barbed wire fencing rules, correcting the numbering so chain link fencing around industrial properties keeps its own subsection.
fe2baf437c027acc.impact: Fence rules stay as they are until the council acts. The correction matters most to industrial property owners and to anyone reading the code to work out which fence is allowed where.
